Prepared is backed by a16z and General Catalyst and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. The company runs a hosted dispatch console at preparedapp.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Kaizen Labs
providers.description: Kaizen Labs is a New York City based govtech company founded in 2022 that builds modern, AI-native software for America's essential public services. Its modular SaaS platform helps local, state, and federal agencies replace legacy systems and deliver resident-facing digital services across recreation and facility reservations, permitting and licensing, DMV and licensing workflows, parking management, tolls, public transportation fare collection, e-billing and tax payments, citations, and judicial court services. The platform is a single, hyper-configurable framework reported to reach more than 40 million residents across 50+ agencies in 17 states. Kaizen Labs is backed by NEA, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Accel, 776, and Carpenter Capital. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Kaizen Labs delivers bespoke integrations to public-sector customers and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Public Sector
providers.description: Industry-vertical index for the public-sector / government API landscape across U.S. federal, state, and local levels. Catalogs the federal API gateway api.data.gov (operated by GSA's Technology Transformation Services under the Open Government Data Act of 2018, used by 25 agencies for over 450 APIs), the catalog.data.gov CKAN metadata catalog, headline federal programmatic surfaces (Regulations.gov, Federal Register, GovInfo, SAM.gov, USAspending.gov, Treasury Fiscal Data, Congress.gov, FEC openFEC, api.weather.gov, api.nasa.gov, Census Data API, Bureau of Economic Analysis), state and local infrastructure (Socrata / Tyler Data and Insights, Tyler Technologies courts/ERP/public-safety stack, OpenGov ERP/budgeting/permitting cloud), and the civic-tech layer (OpenStates / Plural Policy, GovTrack, Open Civic Data). Cross-references Kin Lane's 2026-05-05 roundup of 211 U.S. federal agencies and their APIs on apievangelist.com. The catalog focuses on the data-schema shape of a government dataset / agency / regulation record so that civic-tech and enterprise consumers can normalize across federal, state, and local publishers.

providers.name: Second Front Systems
providers.description: Second Front Systems is a public-benefit, venture-backed software company that accelerates government access to emerging technologies for the world's democracies. Its 2F Suite delivers DevSecOps and continuous-accreditation tooling for defense and public-sector software teams: 2F Workshop (integrated security and compliance tooling for accredited development), 2F Game Warden (a fully accredited FedRAMP High and DoD ATO DevSecOps platform that fast-tracks commercial software to classified and unclassified government networks in roughly 90 days), and 2F Frontier (edge deployment to disconnected and denied environments). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It exposes no public developer API; its primary technical surface is the Game Warden platform documentation, a compliance Trust Center, and a broad certification posture (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FIPS 140).

providers.name: Transport for NSW Open Data Hub
providers.description: Transport for NSW Open Data Hub is a open data portal open-data portal for Australia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 230 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: National Credit Union Administration
providers.description: Created by the U.S. Congress in 1970, the National Credit Union Administration is an independent federal agency that insures deposits at federally insured credit unions, protects the members who own credit unions, and charters and regulates federal credit unions. NCUA publishes Call Report and Financial Performance data and a Credit Union Locator, but does not currently document a public REST API.

providers.name: PACER Case Locator (PCL)
providers.description: The PACER Case Locator (PCL) is a nationwide index of federal court cases. The public PCL API allows users to programmatically search the PCL for federal cases across U.S. district, bankruptcy, and appellate courts using the same search functionality and dataset as the PCL web application.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq RKLB) is an end-to-end space company providing launch services, spacecraft, satellite components, and on-orbit services. Its Electron rocket is the world's most frequently launched orbital small launch vehicle; the medium-lift Neutron rocket is in development. Rocket Lab Space Systems supplies Photon spacecraft, reaction wheels, star trackers, solar arrays, propulsion, separation systems, and composite structures to civil, national security, and commercial customers. Rocket Lab does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Administration for Community Living (ACL)
providers.description: The Administration for Community Living (ACL) is part of the United States Department of Health and Human Services. ACL works to maximize the independence, well-being, and health of older adults, people with disabilities across the lifespan, and their families and caregivers. The agency administers the Older Americans Act programs, supports disability services through centers for independent living, and maintains the AGing, Independence, and Disability (AGID) Program Data Portal providing publicly accessible datasets on aging and disability programs. ACL also operates the National Institute on Disability, Independent Living and Rehabilitation Research (NIDILRR).

providers.description: The Federal Student Aid (FSA) office of the U.S. Department of Education provides grants, loans, and work-study funds to eligible students enrolled in college or career school. FSA operates StudentAid.gov as the consumer portal for managing federal student loans, completing the FAFSA, and exploring repayment options. FSA does not currently publish a public, open developer API program; aggregate higher education and aid data is redistributed through the Department of Education's open data programs such as the College Scorecard API.

providers.name: Asset Reality
providers.description: Asset Reality builds end-to-end software infrastructure for the seizure, management, custody, and disposal of both physical and virtual (crypto) assets, purpose-built for law enforcement, defense, and government agencies. Its platform unifies the asset-recovery lifecycle across four solutions — SEIZE, MANAGE, DEPLOY, and ESCROW — replacing clipboard-and-spreadsheet legacy processes with a single system that preserves asset value through investigation, confiscation, forfeiture, and reallocation to public purposes. The company is FCA-authorized to offer crypto custody in the UK, integrates with providers such as Fireblocks and Taxbit, and runs an Academy offering virtual-asset seizure certifications.

providers.name: Merit Systems Protection Board
providers.description: The Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) is an independent quasi-judicial agency that protects federal merit systems against partisan political and other prohibited personnel practices. It safeguards the rights of federal employees and adjudicates employee appeals.

providers.name: Federal Highway Administration
providers.description: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) provides stewardship over the construction, maintenance and preservation of the Nations highways, bridges and tunnels. FHWA also conducts research and provides technical assistance to state and local agencies to improve safety, mobility, and to encourage innovation.

providers.name: American Battle Monuments Commission
providers.description: The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC), established by Congress in 1923, commemorates the service, achievements, and sacrifice of U.S. Armed Forces. ABMC administers and maintains 26 American military cemeteries and 31 memorials, monuments, and markers on foreign soil. The commission maintains a searchable database of more than 200,000 fallen service members buried or commemorated abroad, accessible via the We Remember burial search portal. ABMC is working on a data roadmap to provide open datasets on data.gov per the Foundations for Evidence-based Policymaking Act (2019).

providers.name: Wonderschool
providers.description: Wonderschool is a child care platform that connects families with licensed care and equips providers with software and services to start, operate, and grow their child care programs. It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Delta Regional Authority
providers.description: The Delta Regional Authority (DRA) is a federal-state partnership established in 2000 to promote and encourage economic development of the lower Mississippi River and Alabama Black Belt regions. DRA does not publish a public REST API; this profile indexes the public website, grants information, and program resources.

providers.name: Federal Labor Relations Authority
providers.description: The Federal Labor Relations Authority oversees the Federal service labor-management relations program. It administers the law that protects the right of employees of the Federal Government to organize, bargain collectively, and participate through labor organizations of their own choosing in decisions affecting them.

providers.name: National Transportation Safety Board
providers.description: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent federal agency responsible for investigating transportation accidents, including those involving airplanes, trains, ships, and pipelines. The NTSB promotes safety and prevents future accidents by conducting thorough investigations and making recommendations to improve safety standards.

providers.name: OffenderList
providers.description: OffenderList is a comprehensive online platform that provides information about individuals who have been convicted of criminal offenses. The website allows users to search for offenders based on various criteria such as name, location, or offense type. OffenderList provides important details about each offender, including their mugshot, charges, conviction date, and sentence length. OffenderList provides security and information-focused organizations API access, batch requests, remote access, and internal access to a national sex offender database.

providers.name: Voatz
providers.description: Voatz is a remote voting technology company providing secure, mobile-based voting for public elections and organizational governance. Voters cast ballots from a smartphone, tablet, or web browser, with identity assured through hardware-backed authentication and biometric verification, ballots anchored to a permissioned blockchain, and a voter-verifiable paper audit trail produced for every vote. The platform pairs the voter-facing mobile app with an administrative dashboard for election officials and supports accessibility features for voters with disabilities. Voatz has run elections across seven countries for more than five million voters, with pilots and deployments for U.S. counties (West Virginia, Utah County, Denver), political parties, and international election authorities. The company is a Techstars-backed startup. Voatz publishes no public developer API; its surface is a security, audit, and disclosure program rather than an integration platform.

providers.name: Md Ally
providers.description: MD Ally is a New York-based digital health company that integrates telehealth into the 911 emergency response system. Its platform lets emergency dispatchers route low-acuity, non-emergency callers to a virtual care tier, connecting patients with telehealth clinicians, in-network resources, and social services instead of dispatching EMS or defaulting to an emergency-room visit. MD Ally works with public safety agencies and payers to expand traditional two-tier dispatch models, reduce unnecessary ambulance transports and ER visits, and improve patient navigation. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars.

providers.name: Drug Enforcement Administration
providers.description: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Registration File API for Web Developers (on the Internet) (25,000 Inquiries). DEA25000. Publication Date: 2006: Page Count: 0: Abstract: The DEA API (Application Program Interface) enables a programmer to develop a program for a specific platform and integrate the DEA data into their verification system ...

providers.name: Farm Service Agency
providers.description: As directed by the OPEN (Open, Public, Electronic, and Necessary) Government Data Act and through its commitment to United States agriculturalists and interested public, FSA provides numerous data resources through reports, visualizations, and other formats.

providers.name: Ginnie Mae
providers.description: The Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) is a government corporation within the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), established in 1968 following the privatization of Fannie Mae. Its mission is to expand mortgage funding insured or guaranteed by federal agencies. By providing a full-faith-and-credit guarantee on securities backed by these mortgages, Ginnie Mae reduces investor risk and broadens the market for mortgage-backed securities.

providers.name: National Invasive Species Information Center
providers.description: National Invasive Species Information Center (NISIC) is the gateway to invasive species information covering federal, state, local, and international sources. Invasive species are plants, animals, or pathogens that are non-native to the ecosystem under consideration, and whose introduction causes or is likely to cause harm.

providers.name: National Pesticide Information Center
providers.description: The National Pesticide Information Center (NPIC) provides objective, science-based information about pesticides and their potential health and environmental effects. NPIC is a cooperative agreement between Oregon State University and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, serving the general public, health professionals, and pesticide manufacturers.

providers.name: Office of Child Support Services
providers.description: The Office of Child Support Services is a government agency that works to ensure that children receive the financial support they need from their non-custodial parent. This office helps establish legal paternity, locate absent parents, and establish and enforce child support orders. They work with both custodial and non-custodial parents to facilitate the collection and distribution of child support payments, ensuring that children have the resources they need to thrive.

providers.name: Office of Community Oriented Policing Services
providers.description: The Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office) is a component of the U.S. Department of Justice that works to advance the practice of community policing in law enforcement agencies across the country. The COPS Office provides grants, resources, and technical assistance to help law enforcement agencies develop and implement community policing strategies that build trust and collaboration with the communities they serve.

providers.name: Office of Congressional Workplace Rights
providers.description: The Office of Congressional Workplace Rights is responsible for enforcing workplace rights for employees of the United States Congress. This includes overseeing the administration of laws such as the Congressional Accountability Act, which guarantees certain rights and protections for congressional staff members.

providers.name: Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management
providers.description: The Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management is a division of the U.S. Department of Energy that is focused on addressing the challenges of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and advancing clean energy technologies. The office works to develop and deploy technologies that can capture, store, and utilize carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel sources, such as coal and natural gas.

providers.name: Graffer
providers.description: Graffer, Inc. (株式会社グラファー) is a Tokyo-based GovTech and generative-AI company founded in 2017 whose mission is to change behavior and society through the power of products. It operates two pillars: the Graffer Platform, a suite of digital-government services for municipalities and national agencies (Smart Application for online applications, Procedure Guide, Window Reservation, and Graffer Call AI voice guidance), adopted by 179+ Japanese municipalities including Fukuoka, Sapporo, Kyoto, and Oita; and Graffer AI Solution, a generative-AI adoption offering for enterprises (consulting, training, and the Graffer AI Studio product). Graffer also runs the citizen-facing お悩みハンドブック benefits-discovery service and the Govtech Trends media. In 2023 it entered a capital and business alliance with Change Holdings. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: International Development Finance Corporation
providers.description: The United States International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is a development finance institution and agency of the United States federal government. DFC invests in development projects primarily in lower and middle-income countries, providing secure private investment opportunities for emerging markets. DFC does not currently expose a public developer API portal; transaction-level data is published as downloadable datasets.

providers.name: Govini
providers.description: Govini (rebranded to Air, air.ai, in 2026) is a defense-technology and decision-analytics company whose Ark platform combines proprietary defense acquisition data with AI-enabled applications to close the national-security "Readiness Gap" across supply chain, science and technology, production, sustainment, logistics, and modernization missions. Ark holds FedRAMP High authorization and a DISA Impact Level 5 (IL5) Provisional Authorization plus service-level IL5 ATOs, making it a closed, government-authorized SaaS platform rather than a public developer API. Led by CEO Tara Murphy Dougherty and backed by investors including Accel and Bain Capital. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and has been enriched with the provider's real public identity, security posture, and published compliance authorizations.

providers.name: NDBC — National Data Buoy Center
providers.description: The NOAA National Data Buoy Center (NDBC) operates a global network of over 1,000 moored buoys, drifting buoys, Coastal-Marine Automated Network (C-MAN) stations, and partner stations that continuously measure and transmit meteorological and oceanographic conditions. Real-time and historical data — wind direction and speed, wave height and period, sea surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, air temperature, dew point, visibility, and salinity — are distributed freely via HTTP file URLs, a THREDDS/OPeNDAP server (NetCDF), an RSS observation feed, and a latest-observations snapshot updated every five minutes. No API key or authentication is required; data is in the public domain under U.S. government open-data policy.

providers.name: Page
providers.description: Page is an AI-powered government relations (GR) platform that tracks legislation, regulatory activity, and policy developments across 70+ jurisdictions in real time. It provides bill tracking, regulatory affairs monitoring, live hearing and vote alerts, lobbying and parliamentary questions data, smart alerts, AI analysis of policy trends, and detailed politician and staff directories, alongside Wonk — an AI assistant for policy research and document generation. Page serves enterprises, multi-client firms, law firms, government agencies, associations, and nonprofits. It is headquartered in Washington, DC with an additional office in Waterloo, Ontario, and is backed by Canaan Partners. Page holds SOC 2 Type II certification. providers.name: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)
providers.description: The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) is part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health and supports research into the causes, treatment, and prevention of arthritis and musculoskeletal and skin diseases. NIAMS publishes health information, research resources, and grant data via its website.

providers.name: Autonomous Cyber
providers.description: Autonomous Cyber is the maker of FUZZ-E, an AI-powered platform for offensive cybersecurity marketed as "The AI Platform for Hacking." It equips commercial and government red teams with deep reconnaissance to uncover hard-to-find bugs and compromise networks, adaptive tooling that responds to AI-enabled defenses by building custom capabilities per engagement, and integrated intelligence workflows that consolidate data and toolkits inside the platform. The company states it operates strictly in the American national interest. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Countable
providers.description: Countable was a civic-engagement technology company backed by Canaan Partners (seed, partner Joydeep Bhattacharyya) that built a digital platform helping citizens understand what Congress was doing in Washington and contact their elected representatives directly, later extending the same advocacy tooling to organizations and brands. As of this enrichment pass the Countable brand is no longer operating independently: both countable.com and countable.us HTTP 302 to https://www.myactionable.com/, the home of Actionable, a self-service advocacy campaign platform made by CSAG that offers petitions, pledges, lawmaker-message campaigns, supporter video collection, lead capture, polling and in-platform real-time campaign reporting on a $29.99/month self-service plan. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, package, webhook catalog, MCP server or /.well-known discovery surface was found on either the legacy Countable hosts or the successor Actionable host during this pass.

providers.name: Mon Ami
providers.description: Mon Ami is a modern data management platform built for aging and disability services providers. It unifies case management, billing and claims, information and assistance (resource directory and intake), enhanced assessments, Older Americans Act reporting (OAAPS), long-term care ombudsman workflows, a provider portal, and Medicaid administrative claiming in one connected system. Mon Ami serves state units on aging, area agencies on aging, intellectual and developmental disabilities programs, Medicaid HCBS providers, and ombudsman programs, helping them reduce administrative burden while improving outcome documentation and compliance reporting. The platform references HL7/FHIR interoperability with EHRs, managed care organizations, and state systems. Mon Ami is a Felicis portfolio company; it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: SAP America
providers.description: SAP America, Inc. is the US subsidiary of SAP SE, headquartered in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and serving as the Americas headquarters for the parent company's enterprise software portfolio (ERP, SCM, CRM, HCM, analytics, and cloud platform). SAP America itself does not publish a US-specific developer portal or APIs distinct from the parent SAP SE surface — all API documentation, SDKs, and OpenAPI artifacts are catalogued under the sibling `sap` repository (api.sap.com, SAP Business Accelerator Hub, SAP BTP). This repo is a subsidiary placeholder that exists to (1) record SAP America as a distinct US legal entity for partnership, public-sector, procurement, and FedRAMP / GovCloud contexts, and (2) cross-link to related US-only sibling subsidiaries — most importantly SAP NS2 (SAP National Security Services), the independent US subsidiary that operates SAP workloads in the Cloud Intelligence Enterprise (CIE), the DoD cloud environment, and the Commercially Regulated Environment (CRE) for federal, defense, and intelligence community customers. No tier-1 API artifacts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, capabilities, plans, rate limits, FinOps) are generated in this repo per the api-evangelist no-empty-artifact rule — they are maintained under the parent `sap` repo and the per-product child repos (`sap-business-technology-platform`, `sap-successfactors`, `sap-ariba`, `sap-concur`, `sap-fieldglass`, `sap-api-management`, `sap-integration-suite`).

providers.name: Election Assistance Commission
providers.description: The U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) was established by the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA). The EAC is an independent, bipartisan commission charged with developing guidance to meet HAVA requirements, adopting voluntary voting system guidelines, and serving as a national clearinghouse of information on election administration. The EAC also accredits testing laboratories, certifies voting systems, and audits the use of HAVA funds. The EAC publishes the Election Administration and Voting Survey (EAVS) datasets and operates an RSS news feed; it does not publish a formal developer API.

providers.name: Federal Bureau of Prisons
providers.description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is responsible for the custody and care of federal inmates in the United States. The BOP operates the inmate locator and publishes facility information online but does not currently offer a public, documented developer API.

providers.name: National Endowment for the Humanities
providers.description: The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is the nation's largest public funder of the humanities, which include history, philosophy, literature, language, ethics, law, archaeology, political theory, comparative religion, anthropology, sociology, and media and cultural studies. NEH does not publish a fully documented public REST API, but it offers a Funded Project Query Form API and bulk XML datasets covering all grants awarded since 1965, plus evaluator and panelist information from 1988 onward.

providers.name: CACI International
providers.description: CACI International provides information technology, professional services, and managed solutions to U.S. federal government agencies in the defense, intelligence, homeland security, and civilian markets. The company delivers expertise and technology across C3I, cyber, digital solutions, enterprise IT, mission support, space, and spectrum superiority domains.

providers.name: Verdant
providers.description: Verdant is an AI-native land-use permitting and planning software platform for local governments, spanning the entire process from a resident's first question through plan review to a commission's final vote. Applicants file complete, compliant applications upfront, and Verdant's AI reads documents, site plans, and diagrams to flag issues and draft staff review reports that municipal staff can approve. The platform is modular, letting jurisdictions buy only the modules they need, configured to their ordinances, workflows, and forms, and includes ordinance-research tooling to benchmark against peer jurisdictions and find gaps in local codes. Verdant is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company; it currently ships an application product for cities and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Liveu
providers.description: LiveU is a provider of cloud-based, IP-bonded live video contribution, production, and distribution technology for broadcasters, sports, news, public safety, and enterprise. Its portfolio spans field encoders (the LU-series and the Q Era LU900Q), the LiveU Central cloud management platform, LiveU Studio and Nexus production tools, the LiveU Matrix distribution grid, DataBridge and LU-LINK connectivity, and the LiveU Solo streaming line. LiveU pioneered bonded-cellular transmission that aggregates multiple LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, and satellite links into a single reliable, low-latency video feed. This profile was surfaced as a venture-capital portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; LiveU publishes marketing, support, and training surfaces but no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or open API documentation was found - the LiveU Central API is available to customers behind authentication.

providers.name: Clear Ballot
providers.description: Clear Ballot Group, Inc. is an election technology company that builds transparent, verifiable voting systems for election administrators across the United States. Its flagship ClearVote platform spans vote-by-mail processing, in-person voting, ballot design, and independent post-election audit and results-verification software, alongside offerings for ranked-choice voting and elections-as-a-service. Clear Ballot operates as a closed, certified election-systems vendor rather than a public API platform, so this profile is identity- and security-focused: it captures the company's public web presence, domain-security posture, and its published vulnerability-disclosure program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Premise
providers.description: Premise is a global data-intelligence platform that combines machine learning with a distributed network of on-the-ground human contributors to collect, structure, and analyze local ground-truth data across 140+ countries. The platform reports 6M+ contributors, 25M+ submissions per year, and 2.3M+ unique points of interest, and serves three primary markets: precision mapping and geospatial intelligence, international development, and public-sector organizations. Premise is a portfolio company of a16z, Anthemis, and GV. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; data is delivered through managed engagements and its customer platform.

providers.name: United States Botanic Garden
providers.description: The United States Botanic Garden (USBG) is a living museum in Washington, D.C. that showcases a diverse collection of plants from around the world. Established by the U.S. Congress in 1820, the Botanic Garden serves as a resource for education and inspiration, promoting an understanding and appreciation of plants and their importance to the environment and human well-being. The Garden maintains more than 9,500 accessions representing approximately 44,000 plants, managed through its Living Collections database (BG-BASE). The USBG is administered by the Architect of the Capitol and is located adjacent to the U.S. Capitol on the National Mall.

providers.name: GoTenna
providers.description: goTenna is a mobile mesh networking company that builds off-grid, long-range communication hardware and software. Its consumer goTenna Mesh and professional goTenna Pro devices pair with smartphones over Bluetooth to relay text messages, GPS locations, and data across a decentralized VHF/UHF radio mesh with no cell towers, wifi, or satellite dependency. The Aspen Grove mesh protocol stack and the Radio SDK (RSDK) let third-party developers embed goTenna radio connectivity into Android, iOS, and Linux JVM applications for public safety, defense, and outdoor use. goTenna exposes no public REST/web API; developer integration is via the native RSDK, which requires an SDK app token obtained from goTenna.

providers.name: Kaizen
providers.description: Kaizen Labs is a New York City civic-technology company building a modular platform that helps local, state, and federal government agencies serve constituents simply, securely, and at scale. Founded in 2022 by Nikhil Reddy and Kj Shah, the platform spans permitting and licensing, recreation reservations and registrations, parking management, tolls and transit fare collection, e-billing and tax payments, DMV and judicial-court services, and AI-assisted case management — reaching roughly 40 million residents across 50+ agencies in 17 states. Kaizen has raised about $35M from NEA, Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, 776, and Carpenter Capital. The company publishes no public developer API surface; this profile is enriched from its public website, llms.txt, and security & compliance disclosures.

providers.name: Defense Information System for Security
providers.description: The Defense Information System for Security (DISS) is the enterprise-wide Department of Defense system of record for personnel security, suitability, and credentialing management for military, civilian, and contractor personnel. Operated by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), DISS replaced the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS) as the system of record on March 31, 2021. DISS is restricted to authorized DoD and federal users and contractor security officers; it does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: United States European Command
providers.description: United States European Command (EUCOM) is one of the eleven unified combatant commands of the U.S. Department of Defense. EUCOM is responsible for U.S. military operations and security cooperation in Europe, as well as parts of North Africa and the Middle East. The command works to support NATO allies, deter aggression, and ensure regional stability through military exercises, humanitarian operations, and partnership activities. EUCOM does not expose public-facing REST APIs; access to EUCOM data systems requires DoD Common Access Card (CAC) authentication through restricted portals including the EUCOM intranet portal and milSuite collaboration platform.

providers.name: ClassWallet
providers.description: ClassWallet is a patented digital wallet and public-funds disbursement platform used by government agencies, school districts, and program administrators to distribute, control, and reconcile public money. Recipients access and spend allocated funds online or in-store while administrators get spending controls, approved marketplaces, reimbursement workflows, direct vendor payments (DirectPay), and audit-ready reporting and compliance. ClassWallet powers K-12 education programs, Education Savings Accounts (ESAs), scholarships and grants, government assistance, and vocational rehabilitation initiatives. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes product and program surfaces but no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Graylark
providers.description: Graylark is an AI-powered geolocation intelligence company serving law enforcement, government, and enterprise customers. Its technology extracts location data from ordinary images at varying levels of precision, marketed under the GeoSpy brand (geospy.ai). The platform offers Global Search (1-50 km accuracy with worldwide coverage), Street Search (meter-level precision across 1,000+ cities), and Property Search (100+ million records for matching a scene to a specific structure). Graylark positions these capabilities for investigations, fraud detection, insurance validation, and journalistic verification of visual content. Access is gated to qualified government and enterprise organizations via a contact-sales/licensing model; the company publishes no public self-service API, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Pavilion
providers.description: Pavilion is a government purchasing platform that helps public-sector buyers find vendors, get quotes, and buy what they need without the guesswork. It connects procurement teams at 3,500+ SLED (state, local, and education) agencies with qualified vendors, surfaces the most direct compliant route to purchase based on each agency's rules and existing cooperative contracts, and lets vendors claim a free supplier profile to get discovered. The product is 100% free for public agencies. Pavilion is a SaaS marketplace backed by Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: PSD Citywide
providers.description: PSD Citywide is a SaaS provider of enterprise asset management (EAM) and public-sector software for North American municipalities and government organizations. Its integrated Citywide platform spans asset management, maintenance and work-order management, GIS integration (ESRI-powered mapping), permitting, planning and licensing with citizen portals, multi-year budgeting and forecasting, facility/space management (Spaces), and a field mobile app, alongside asset-management advisory and grant services. The homepage references a "robust API" for integration and customization, but no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found during enrichment; end-user product documentation is published in a HappyFox-powered help center. Added to the API Evangelist network via the norwest-venture-partners portfolio.

providers.name: GovGuard
providers.description: GovGuard is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) GovTech company building AI infrastructure for government agencies, starting with Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request automation. Its AI agents route incoming public-records requests, search across municipal archives (emails, meeting minutes, PDFs, and shared drives), flag personally identifiable information and other exempt material for redaction against the relevant state exemption codes, and draft response letters for clerk review while maintaining a complete audit trail. Agencies retain full ownership and control of all records and metadata, and GovGuard states that it does not train models on client data. The company was founded by Aditya Sabharwal and Gleb Hulting and is based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Brain
providers.description: Brain Co. builds agent-native operating systems for institutions across the public and private sectors. Its Atlas platform powers GovOS — permitting, licensing, claims, and casework for government agencies at national scale — and InsuranceOS for underwriting, claims, authorization, and insurance operations, with an emphasis on sovereign-grade security and vendor neutrality. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the company was cofounded by Elad Gil, Jared Kushner, and Luis Videgaray, with a team drawn from Google, DeepMind, NVIDIA, Palantir, and Tesla. Brain Co. does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definitions; this profile tracks its public web surface (news, trust center, privacy and terms) pending any future developer program.

providers.name: Vector Solutions
providers.description: Vector Solutions is a SaaS provider of industry-specific training, operational readiness, workforce management, and risk-management software. Its portfolio spans Learning Management Systems (LMS), Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) management, staff scheduling, incident and equipment tracking, professional development and evaluation management, and large online course libraries. The company serves education (K-12 and higher ed), public safety (fire, EMS, law enforcement), government, manufacturing, construction, and gaming markets, helping organizations prepare their people, stay in compliance, and manage operational risk. Vector Solutions is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It runs a GraphQL endpoint at api.vectorsolutions.com/graphql that backs its applications; that endpoint is live but not publicly documented and has schema introspection disabled.

providers.name: Montenegro Open Data
providers.description: Montenegro Open Data is a national government open-data portal for Montenegro running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 894 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: AAR Corp
providers.description: AAR Corp is a global aerospace and defense aftermarket solutions company and the number one aviation maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) provider in North America. They offer aircraft parts supply, airframe and component MRO, integrated software solutions (Trax, Aerostrat, Airinmar), and expeditionary services to commercial airlines and government customers worldwide.

providers.name: Biobot
providers.description: Biobot Analytics is a wastewater epidemiology company that operates a wastewater intelligence platform, analyzing sewage samples to detect and track more than 50 human health indicators — including pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza, RSV, measles, norovirus), substances (fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, buprenorphine), and public-health threats (HIV, mpox, poliovirus, Candida auris) — before they surface in conventional reporting. Founded from MIT research and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Biobot serves federal, state, and local government agencies, pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, and healthcare systems through dashboards, CSV exports, map visualizations, and enterprise data integrations. Biobot does not publish a public self-serve developer API; data access is arranged directly with the company.

providers.name: Mechanical Orchard
providers.description: Mechanical Orchard is an enterprise software company, founded by Pivotal veterans, that modernizes mission-critical legacy and mainframe systems. Its flagship platform, Imogen, uses AI to observe how legacy applications actually behave, then incrementally rewrites them into modern, cloud-ready code while continuously verifying that behavior is preserved so nothing breaks during migration. The company pairs the Imogen platform with professional services and a free proof of concept, integrates with AWS Transform and Google Cloud, and serves both commercial enterprises and government agencies looking to retire risky COBOL and mainframe estates. It is backed by Bloomberg Beta, Emergence Capital, and GV.

providers.name: Government Accountability Office
providers.description: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) is the United States government's supreme audit institution. It provides Congress with auditing, evaluation, and investigative services, and publishes reports, testimonies, and other products examining federal programs and policies.

providers.name: Parsons Corporation
providers.description: Parsons Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Parsons Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: HAAS Alert
providers.description: HAAS Alert operates Safety Cloud, a connected-vehicle safety platform that delivers real-time digital alerts to nearby motorists about active emergency responses, roadside hazards, work zones, stopped vehicles, and slow-moving equipment. Using vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and cellular messaging, Safety Cloud gives drivers up to roughly 30 seconds of advance warning to help reduce collisions with first responders, tow operators, and roadway workers. HAAS Alert integrates with telematics platforms, fleet manufacturers, OEM vehicles, in-car navigation (including Waze), and roadway infrastructure to form a large connected-vehicle alerting ecosystem. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from HAAS Alert's public web surface; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs were found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Calvis
providers.description: Calvis is a multi-agency security guard marketplace that connects businesses with vetted, state-licensed, background-checked security guards from multiple professional agencies across 40+ US cities. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Miami, Florida, the platform pairs on-demand booking with AI-powered deployment matching, real-time GPS tracking and geofencing, live AI coaching delivered to guards through an earpiece, and automated incident reporting and site analytics. Businesses book unarmed, armed, event, retail, construction, corporate, residential, hospital, cannabis, and school security through the web platform and iOS/Android apps, while security professionals join the network to find work. Calvis is backed by Version One Ventures.

providers.name: Biobot Analytics
providers.description: Biobot Analytics is a wastewater intelligence company that measures human health signals in sewage to deliver population-level public health data. Founded out of MIT in 2017, Biobot analyzes wastewater samples for pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza, RSV, mpox), substances (opioids and other drugs), and other biomarkers, turning them into de-identified, community-scale intelligence. It serves federal government, state and local government, pharmaceutical and life-science organizations, healthcare systems, and wastewater treatment plants, who access results and dashboards through Biobot's customer data-exploration platform. Biobot is a venture-backed company in the DCVC portfolio. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; Biobot delivers data via reports and a login-gated platform rather than an open API program.

providers.name: BridgeCare Finance
providers.description: BridgeCare (getbridgecare.com) is an integrated, modular software platform for the early care and education (ECE) system. It gives state agencies, cities and counties, child care resource and referral organizations (CCR&Rs), nonprofits, and school districts one system to run Pre-K program administration, family navigation, coordinated eligibility and enrollment, centralized eligibility screening, licensing, workforce development, quality management (QRIS), grants management, subsidy administration, tri-share administration, and program assurance. The platform is used by 500,000+ families, 50,000+ providers, and 500+ counties. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, BridgeCare is backed by Techstars and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. BridgeCare operates an API host but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer documentation, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Defense Contract Audit Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), under the authority, direction, and control of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller), provides audit and financial advisory services to Department of Defense and other federal entities responsible for acquisition and contract administration. DCAA publishes guidance, audit programs, and reports through its website but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Contract Management Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) is the Department of Defense component that works directly with defense suppliers to help ensure that DoD, federal, and allied government supplies and services are delivered on time, at projected cost, and meet performance requirements. DCMA performs contract administration, quality assurance, and earned value management oversight, but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service
providers.description: The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) is the agency within the Department of Defense responsible for paying members of the U.S. military, DoD civilian employees, contractors, and annuitants, as well as providing finance and accounting services to DoD components and other federal agencies. DFAS exposes member-facing self-service portals such as myPay but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Amentum
providers.description: Amentum Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: AMTM) is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions company serving U.S. federal customers across defense, intelligence, energy, space, and civilian missions, with allied work in the United Kingdom and Australia. The company was created from the spin-off of AECOM's Management Services business in 2020, and on September 27, 2024 completed a Reverse Morris Trust transaction with Jacobs Solutions to merge Jacobs' Critical Mission Solutions (CMS) and Cyber & Intelligence (C&I) businesses into Amentum. Post-merger Amentum reports approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenue, a $47.1 billion backlog, ~53,000 employees in 80 countries, and is headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia. The business is organized around six capability areas — Mission Modernization & Sustainment, Space Systems, Digital Transformation, Sustainability & Environment, Advanced Energy Solutions, and Data Analytics & Cyber. Most delivery occurs under contract through classified, CAC-gated, or program portals; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or REST API has been identified.

providers.name: Ethos Systems
providers.description: Ethos Systems is an AI-powered human readiness platform that unifies learning, performance, and outcomes management in a single system built for enterprise and government deployment across both commercial and classified networks. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Ethos delivers personalized training with algorithm-driven interventions, rapid AI content development, and real-time readiness dashboards that connect learning to operational outcomes. It serves the U.S. military, federal civilian agencies, life sciences, manufacturing, freight and logistics, hospitality, athletics, utilities, insurance, and government contractors, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the Westly Group, and Pear VC. The company operates the Ethos and Learn to Win platforms; its developer and product documentation is gated behind authentication and it exposes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Toka
providers.description: Toka is a defense and intelligence technology company, founded in 2017-2018 and headquartered in Maryland with R&D in Israel, that develops signals intelligence, ISR, cyber operations, and force protection capabilities exclusively for militaries, homeland security organizations, intelligence agencies, and law enforcement in the United States and allied nations. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Eclipse Ventures, and Dell Technologies Capital, Toka sells government-facing capability platforms and cyber capacity-building services rather than a public developer or API surface, and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.
