providers.name: SpryPoint
providers.description: SpryPoint is a cloud-based customer service and operations software provider for utilities, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, Canada. Its platform modernizes the meter-to-cash lifecycle for water & sewer, electric, and gas utilities across North America through an integrated suite of modules: SpryCIS (customer information system), SpryEngage (omnichannel customer portal), SpryWallet (payment processing), SpryMobile MFS (field service orders), SpryMobile WOAM (work order and asset management), SpryBackflow (backflow compliance), and SpryIDM (interval data management). The company serves 100+ utility clients, employs 285+ people, is SOC 2 audited, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Insight Partners. SpryPoint publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; integrations are delivered through partnership engagements rather than a self-service API.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: True Anomaly
providers.description: True Anomaly is a defense-technology company building spacecraft, software, and payloads for space superiority. Its products include Jackal, a multirole space-superiority platform positioned as a tactical fighter-interceptor for contested orbital environments, and Mosaic, an autonomy software platform that transforms commander intent into autonomous action. The company serves U.S. government and allied defense customers from facilities in Centennial and Colorado Springs, Colorado; Long Beach, California; and Washington, DC. True Anomaly publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its only machine-readable public surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-disclosure contact.

providers.name: Civica Digital
providers.description: Cívica Digital is a Mexican civic-technology company, founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, that helps governments, public institutions, and organizations design, build, and launch digital services for citizens. Its product portfolio includes Urbem, a platform for digitizing government procedures and citizen-facing services; Signum, a digital document and official-records management system with electronic signatures; and a suite of conversational AI agents that support citizens over WhatsApp, phone, and web. The company focuses on digital government transformation across Latin America. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's public web presence, legal pages, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Darwin
providers.description: Darwin AI is an AI governance platform built exclusively for state, local, and education (SLED) government agencies, providing a centralized, secure hub for the public sector to safely adopt, manage, and govern AI tools while ensuring compliance, accountability, and public records requirements are met. The platform serves IT departments, innovation and digital services teams, city and county management, and data governance professionals across municipal and state government. Its core product surface includes the Control Center, which delivers cross-departmental visibility into AI usage along with records management and FOIA compliance tracking; the Policy Wizard, which helps agencies establish and refine AI policies aligned to regulatory requirements using 30+ policy frameworks and 15+ city and county regulation packs; Risk Management, which detects unauthorized or unvetted AI applications; the AI Navigator, which monitors departmental adoption patterns and surfaces actionable insights; and the Marketplace, an organization-wide hub of approved AI applications. Darwin AI was named to Government Technology's 2026 GovTech 100. The company also publishes a free public Policy Wizard tool. Darwin is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a government-sector company profile. As of this enrichment pass Darwin publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Indigov
providers.description: Indigov is a constituent relationship management (CRM) platform purpose-built for government — U.S. Congressional offices, state legislatures, and municipal agencies — that unifies inbound constituent communications from email, web forms, SMS, social media, phone, and scanned mail into a single cross-organizational inbox. It layers casework tracking, constituent routing, smart tagging, and mass-email triage with rapid response, plus a customer data platform for sentiment and engagement analytics and an award-winning mobile app for field staff. Indigov serves government offices across 35 states and 2 territories and was acquired by Granicus, joining its Government Experience Cloud (GXC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Amber Box
providers.description: AmberBox is an indoor gunshot detection company (San Francisco, CA) that builds sensor hardware and a response platform for schools, offices, and public buildings. Its patented tri-factor detection algorithm combines percussion, audio, and infrared signatures to identify a firearm discharge with a near-zero false-alarm rate, then automatically notifies on-site security and law enforcement to cut emergency response time by an average of five minutes. AmberBox integrates with existing physical-security estates (access control, IP video/VMS, PSIM, mass-notification, and fire-alarm-style life-safety systems) via closed-contact relay switches and TCP/IP relay input modules rather than a public developer API. Surfaced as an Uncork Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company publishes no public REST/GraphQL API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Rohirrim
providers.description: Rohirrim is an AI-native Unified Acquisition Platform that automates and accelerates government procurement for both agencies and contractors. Its UnifiedAcquire product helps government agencies manage procurements from market research through award by automating acquisition documents and centralizing institutional knowledge, while UnifiedRespond (RohanRFP) helps companies identify, match, and draft RFP responses faster and at lower cost. The company targets federal agencies, government contractors, Fortune 500 firms, and healthcare organizations, and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Insight Partners. Rohirrim publishes no public developer API surface today; this profile captures its public web, content, and security-posture footprint.

providers.name: The Atlas Marketplace
providers.description: The Atlas Marketplace (branded "The Atlas") is a free online community and knowledge marketplace for local government leaders. Officials and staff use it to learn from their peers about the smart, safe, and sustainable solutions working in their communities, browsing a searchable library of case studies, vendors, and civic-technology projects. The platform connects public-sector practitioners with the companies and partners behind proven municipal solutions across mobility, infrastructure, sustainability, and public safety. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a content and community website rather than a developer/API product; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public web presence.

providers.name: Fannie Mae
providers.description: Fannie Mae, officially known as the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a government-sponsored enterprise that plays a critical role in the American housing market. Established in 1938, Fannie Mae operates as a secondary mortgage lender, purchasing mortgages from banks and other financial institutions. By buying these loans, Fannie Mae helps to provide liquidity to the mortgage market, enabling banks to lend more money to homebuyers. Fannie Mae operates a developer portal that hosts API integrations for mortgage industry partners; access typically requires authenticated business relationships.

providers.name: Regbase
providers.description: Regbase is an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform that helps legal teams, compliance professionals, researchers, and government vendors monitor new and proposed laws worldwide. The platform uses AI agents to identify regulatory changes across 195 countries and 50 US states, surfacing draft bills, consultations, compliance requirements, and opportunities like grants from hard-to-find government sources, non-English publications, and informal channels that traditional tools miss. Regbase then analyzes those changes automatically and alerts users to updates relevant to their practice areas, spanning employment and labor, AI governance, healthcare, privacy, climate and sustainability, government contracting, and other regulated industries. Founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Regbase is based in San Francisco. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist network; at the time of enrichment Regbase publishes a login-only web application and no public API, developer documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: Infilla
providers.description: Infilla is a permitting software platform that modernizes housing approvals for cities and municipal planning departments. Its product suite—a fee Calculator, a guided Application Form for permit intake, and digital Plan Check checklists—cuts response times, eliminates repetitive administrative work, and accelerates housing production. Founded and led by CEO Jenny Song after research with 300+ planners across 50+ jurisdictions, Infilla targets permitting as a major barrier to housing development by equipping government staff to work faster and better serve their communities. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Hidden Level
providers.description: Hidden Level is a U.S.-based defense and aerospace technology company that turns radio-frequency (RF) activity into trusted airspace intelligence. Its passive RF sensing platform detects and tracks unmanned aerial systems (drones) and other activity across air, ground, sea, and space domains without requiring emitters or heavy on-site infrastructure. Hidden Level packages this as hardware sensor platforms, software platforms, and data platforms serving defense and military, critical infrastructure protection, homeland security, and public safety customers. The company hosts its platform on AWS with least-privilege access, MFA, and TLS 1.3 API communications, aligns corporate controls to NIST SP 800-171, and emphasizes U.S. design and manufacturing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hidden Level's public web and security surface; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: ABL Space Systems
providers.description: ABL Space Systems is an American launch vehicle company founded in 2017 by Harry O'Hanley and Dan Piemont, headquartered in El Segundo, California, with operations at the Port of Long Beach, Mojave and Kodiak, Alaska. ABL built RS1, a two-stage, kerosene/liquid-oxygen small satellite launch vehicle designed to deliver 1,350 kg to low Earth orbit and 1,000 kg to sun-synchronous orbit, powered by nine in-house additively manufactured E2 engines on the first stage and one on the second. Its companion GS0 ground system packages an entire orbital launch site into standard shipping containers so a pad can be activated anywhere with a flat concrete surface and moved by land, sea or air. RS1 attempted its first orbital flight from Pacific Spaceport Complex Kodiak in January 2023 and was lost shortly after liftoff; a second vehicle was destroyed during preflight static-fire testing in July 2024. In November 2024 the company announced its exit from the commercial orbital launch market, and in February 2025 it rebranded as Long Wall, refocusing on containerized missile defense — the Cyclops exoatmospheric interceptor, RSX low-cost liquid boosters for flight testing and threat replication, and the Ironwood ground support equipment line. ABL/Long Wall is an aerospace and defense hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, machine-readable API contract or developer portal.

providers.name: Sierra Space
providers.description: Sierra Space is a commercial space and defense technology company headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, spun out of Sierra Nevada Corporation as an independent entity in April 2021 and building on more than three decades of spaceflight heritage. The company designs and manufactures the Dream Chaser reusable lifting-body spaceplane and Shooting Star cargo module, the LIFE expandable space habitat and the Orbital Reef commercial space station developed with Blue Origin, Eclipse-class satellites for national security and on-orbit servicing missions, VORTEX rocket propulsion and hypersonics, space solar arrays and electrical power systems, environmental control and life support systems, and a broad spaceflight hardware catalog spanning valves, regulators, radiators, sensors, actuators, docking and berthing systems, deployable structures and launch adapters. Sierra Space states it has delivered more than 4,000 space systems, subsystems and components across more than 500 space missions. It is a hardware and mission-systems manufacturer rather than a software platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Tengo
providers.description: Tengo is an AI-powered public procurement platform that helps companies find, evaluate, and respond to public tenders in one place. Founded in 2023 in France by Hugues Renou and Yoann Gauthier, Tengo covers the full tender lifecycle — sourcing and targeting relevant opportunities, drafting and writing proposals with AI, and managing responses and performance analytics — serving SMEs, mid-sized companies, and large corporations. Tengo raised a €3M round led by Point Nine in 2024. It operates a business-user SaaS with a request-a-demo onboarding and no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Atalanta
providers.description: Atalanta is a mathematical AI company building provably correct decision-making for the world's most important missions. Its flagship platform, Argo, is described as the first software understanding platform - it uses mathematical proof and formal verification to establish safety, security, and performance guarantees for software-defined and autonomous systems at operational speed, moving beyond the limits of traditional testing. Argo identifies failure modes before deployment and verifies compliance with critical constraints across energy (nuclear and grid control systems), space (satellite and communications networks), and defense (complex military systems and data isolation). Atalanta was founded by Anjana Rajan and Jonathan Ring, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is backed by Felicis and In-Q-Tel.

providers.name: Opolskie Open Data
providers.description: Opolskie Open Data is a regional government open-data portal for Poland running DKAN.

providers.name: TurbineOne
providers.description: TurbineOne builds a frontline AI/ML platform that turns raw sensor data into real-time detection, classification, and targeting at the edge for defense and national-security missions. Its product suite spans Frontline Perception (edge computer vision on live sensor feeds), Frontline Command, Frontline Autonomy, a Model Hub for managing and deploying ML models, and EdgeWorks, a program that brings warfighters, mission teams, and engineers together to develop and validate mission capabilities for contested, disconnected environments. The company was founded on expertise in artificial intelligence, mesh networking, and sensing technology, and positions its work as "Responsible AI for our nation's heroes." It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. TurbineOne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, GitHub organization, and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Zurich Open Data
providers.description: Zurich Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Switzerland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 925 datasets.

providers.name: Kinside
providers.description: Kinside is a modern child care marketplace that connects families with licensed child care providers by surfacing real-time availability across thousands of providers, helping parents find care in minutes rather than months. Beyond the consumer marketplace, Kinside serves child care providers with enrollment and scheduling tools, employers with child care benefit programs, and government agencies seeking community child care supply-and-demand data. Backed by Initialized Capital and Techstars, the company operates alongside UrbanSitter in the family-care benefits space. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from venture-portfolio discovery; Kinside does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time, so this entry captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: SkySafe
providers.description: SkySafe is a San Diego-based drone-detection and airspace-intelligence company (founded 2015, backed by a16z) whose cloud SaaS platform lets airports, critical infrastructure, law enforcement, universities, correctional facilities, and government customers detect, track, analyze, and act on every drone in their airspace in real time. The platform surfaces precise drone location, altitude, velocity, flight status, launch point, and pilot location, receives and analyzes Remote ID, retains historical flight telemetry for forensic "Prosecutor-Ready" reporting, and pushes instant notifications via SMS, Microsoft Teams, Slack, or CommandCentral Aware. SkySafe advertises integration APIs that push detection, forensics, and analytics into third-party command centers and mitigation workflows, but its developer surface (app.skysafe.io, docs.skysafe.io, api.skysafe.io) sits entirely behind customer authentication — there is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification to harvest.

providers.name: ThayerMahan
providers.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kodiak Networks
providers.description: Kodiak Networks built a carrier-grade Push-to-Talk over Cellular (PoC) platform that wireless operators deployed as their own branded push-to-talk service, competing with legacy land mobile radio for dispatch, field-service and public-safety workforces. Motorola Solutions acquired the company in 2017 and the technology now ships as Motorola Solutions' "Kodiak" mission-critical push-to-talk (MCPTT) offering for carriers, aligned to the 3GPP SA WG6 MCPTT specifications (TS 23.379, TS 24.382, TS 24.482, TS 22.582) and interoperable with land mobile radio through Critical Connect. Kodiak Networks no longer operates independently: its legacy domain serves only a static "Site under maintenance" placeholder over plain HTTP, and it publishes no OpenAPI, developer documentation, SDKs or public API surface of its own. Broadband push-to-talk APIs for third-party integration do exist, but access is gated behind the Motorola Solutions Application Developer Program.

providers.name: Blue Water Autonomy
providers.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Citizen
providers.description: Citizen is a consumer public-safety mobile application that delivers real-time, location-based safety alerts and incident notifications to users about events happening in their communities. The app surfaces verified alerts, live video streamed by witnesses at the scene, incident search, and community broadcast features to help people connect and stay safe. Backed by 8vc, Citizen positions itself as the leading public-safety app in the United States. It is a consumer product with no public developer program, API documentation, SDK, or developer portal exposed on its website as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Conntour
providers.description: Conntour is an Israeli AI video-intelligence company building a natural-language search engine for security camera systems. Its vision and language models let operators search any camera feed in plain language to find any object, person, or situation in real time, raise automatic alerts, and investigate recorded footage in seconds — turning passive surveillance into active intelligence. Unlike legacy analytics that depend on preset object or motion definitions, Conntour's models scale to thousands of concurrent feeds (up to roughly 50 feeds per consumer GPU such as an Nvidia RTX 4090) and deploy fully on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid mix, either augmenting existing VMS/security systems or serving as a standalone surveillance platform. Founded in 2024 by Matan Goldner and Tomer Kola, the company serves intelligence agencies, homeland security, law enforcement, military and defense, transportation, and enterprise customers. It raised a $7M seed round in March 2026 led by General Catalyst, with participation from Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Liquid 2 Ventures.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: LAMMA Toscana Open Data
providers.description: LAMMA Toscana Open Data is a government agency open-data portal for Italy running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 184 datasets from Tuscany's meteorological and environmental research agency.

providers.name: Carahsoft
providers.description: Carahsoft Technology Corp. is a master government IT solutions aggregator and distributor that resells software, cloud, and cybersecurity products from hundreds of technology vendors to U.S. federal, state, local, defense, intelligence, healthcare, and education customers across 220+ government contract vehicles. Carahsoft operates a partner-facing Developer Center that exposes partner integrations for accounts, quotes, orders, invoices, price lists, purchase orders, and resources; the underlying API is gated behind a partner account and is not a public REST API.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.

providers.name: Vannevar Labs
providers.description: Vannevar Labs is a defense technology company that builds agentic AI for national security missions. Its Agent Orchestration platform fuses defense-grade foundational data, mission requirements, and strategic reasoning into mission-focused AI agents — spanning course-of-action, force-protection, information-operations, and cross-border pattern-analysis agents — used from tactical kill-chain decisions to theater-level campaigns. The company collects hard-to-reach data from adversarial information environments to train models for national security, and works across mission areas including Indo-Pacific deterrence, homeland security, and intelligent statecraft. Backed by General Catalyst; no public developer portal or API surface is published.

providers.name: Closure
providers.description: Closure (Closure Intelligence, Inc.) builds an AI-powered digital analyst platform for law enforcement agencies that securely transcribes, translates, searches, organizes, and analyzes case evidence — jail communications, warrant returns, and large multi-lingual case files — to help investigators overcome evidence overload and resolve homicides and cold cases. The platform runs under a zero-access security model with SOC 2 Type II, CJIS, and HIPAA compliance. Backed by CRV. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: GetInsured
providers.description: GetInsured (Vimo, Inc.) is a SaaS technology provider for public-sector healthcare that powers state-based health insurance marketplaces (SBMs). Its platform handles eligibility and enrollment, plan shopping and comparison, and consumer-assistance contact-center operations for state ACA exchanges. GetInsured powers ten state marketplaces (including Idaho, Illinois, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Virginia, and Oregon, with Oregon launching in 2027) and supported the migration of roughly 4.5 million people off Healthcare.gov. It sells to state governments, insurance carriers, agents/brokers, and enrollment assisters. GetInsured does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or API; integrations are delivered under contract. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Cognitive Space
providers.description: Cognitive Space is an aerospace software company delivering AI-powered automated satellite operations for constellation and fleet management. Its CNTIENT.Optimize platform automates mission planning, tasking, and multi-ground-station pass scheduling for satellite operators and government agencies, reporting large per-operator time savings, while CNTIENT.Earth delivers satellite Data-as-a-Service. The company integrates with customer systems via APIs and serves clients including Terran Orbital, the Space Development Agency, the Air Force Research Lab, and NOAA. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Forward Platform
providers.description: FORWARD Platform is a govtech SaaS company (a Techstars portfolio company) offering one secure platform for administering public-benefit programs. It serves governments, nonprofits, and foundations with tooling for program management, online form building, eligibility determination, case management, client communication, referrals, payment disbursement, reporting and analytics, and fraud prevention. FORWARD supports service-delivery programs such as guaranteed basic income, housing assistance, and emergency management, and is packaged in Direct, Pro, Enterprise, and Ally tiers. Enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer portal — this is a product/marketing web presence only.

providers.name: Rebellion Defense
providers.description: Rebellion Defense (rebelliondefense.com) is a defense-technology company building an AI-driven "intelligence shield" for protecting critical infrastructure and military assets — combining multi-band AESA radar sensing (ARGUS/SPECTRUM), AI track-fusion and threat prediction (PRISM), operator alerting and situational awareness (IRIS/STATUS), and effector command-and-control (HADES) on an integrated RBLN-OS platform. Recent public activity includes U.S. Navy contracts and designation as an awardable vendor on the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace. The company publishes a marketing site only: as of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface is exposed. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Castelion
providers.description: Castelion is a vertically integrated defense technology company that designs, tests, and manufactures next-generation military systems, with a focus on affordable, mass-producible hypersonic strike weapons such as its Blackbeard system, built rapidly and at scale to deter future conflict. Founded by former SpaceX and defense-industry engineers, it operates manufacturing and test facilities in Torrance, CA; Rio Rancho, NM; Midland, TX; and Allen, TX. Castelion is privately held and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: L3Harris Technologies
providers.description: L3Harris Technologies is an agile global aerospace and defense technology innovator delivering end-to-end solutions in space, air, land, sea, and cyber domains for government and commercial customers. No publicly documented APIs are available; product integrations are delivered through customer engagements.

providers.name: Fed10
providers.description: Fed10 is a legislative-intelligence and government-affairs platform staffed by AI agents. It continuously monitors legislation across U.S. state legislatures and Congress, flags regulatory threats and opportunities relevant to a company's business, and delivers actionable policy insights — the analysis a $500/hour policy consultant produces in days, returned in seconds. Founded in 2026 by three former lobbyists and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026), Fed10 packages bill tracking, amendment analysis, compliance-gap assessment, and continuous legislative monitoring into an agentic workflow for public-affairs and compliance teams.

providers.name: data.gov.mt (Open Data Malta)
providers.description: data.gov.mt is the national government open-data portal for Malta, operated by MITA (Malta Information Technology Agency) as a bespoke "Shared Data Governance and Data Management Platform" with a JavaScript single-page-app front end (served at portal.data.gov.mt / open.data.gov.mt). It is DCAT-AP-compliant for EU harvesting (~230+ datasets) but exposes no publicly documented JSON catalog API. Malta's geospatial APIs are available separately via the MSDI geoportal.

providers.name: Dream
providers.description: Dream (Dream Security / Dream Group) is an AI company for national cybersecurity and sovereign AI, founded in 2023 by Shalev Hulio, former Austrian Chancellor Sebastian Kurz, and Gil Dolev, with offices in Tel Aviv, Vienna, and Abu Dhabi. Dream builds a full sovereign AI stack that nations own, control, and operate with zero foreign reliance, delivered on-premises and air-gapped with no foreign telemetry. Its platform spans three products: Atlas, a national AI platform that turns government data into knowledge and decisions across intelligence, finance, health, and supply chain; Sphere, a unified cyber-defense system protecting government and critical infrastructure against nation-state threats; and Hero, an autonomous multi-agent solution for vulnerability discovery and patching. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and others at a multibillion-dollar valuation, Dream has no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Pano
providers.description: Pano AI provides enterprise-grade, AI-powered wildfire and bushfire detection. The platform combines ultra-high-definition 360-degree mountaintop cameras, satellite feeds, field sensor data, and machine learning to detect ignitions early, confirm and triangulate their location, and deliver real-time visual situational intelligence to utilities, fire agencies, first responders, and landowners. Operators access the Pano 360 platform at 360.pano.ai to monitor camera networks, review AI detections, and coordinate incident response. Backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital, Pano was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Sensemesh
providers.description: Sensemesh builds an AI-powered operating system that unifies cameras, sensors, and drones into a single intelligent network for real-time perception and autonomous response. The platform fuses visual, thermal, audio, and pressure sensor data so organizations can detect threats, investigate incidents, dispatch drones autonomously, and query sensor history in natural language across law enforcement, corrections and prisons, events and venues, homeowners associations, and schools and universities. Backed by DCVC, Sensemesh was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single marketing site (sensemesh.ai) with no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or well-known metadata.

providers.name: data.egov.bg (Open Data Portal of Bulgaria)
providers.description: data.egov.bg is the national government open-data portal for Bulgaria, operated by the Ministry of e-Government (Министерство на електронното управление). It is a custom Laravel application exposing a REST API with action-style endpoints (predominantly POST with JSON bodies) under the /api prefix. It is not CKAN. Public read endpoints require no key; write/admin endpoints require an api_key obtained via a free account.

providers.name: data.gov.hr
providers.description: data.gov.hr (Portal otvorenih podataka) is the national government open-data portal for Croatia, operated by the Ministry of Justice and Public Administration. It runs CKAN 2.9.9 and exposes the standard CKAN Action API over approximately 3,858 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access, plus DCAT-AP RDF/XML catalog feeds for EU harvesting. Note that the CKAN API is mounted under a non-default /ckan/ path prefix; root-level CKAN URLs return the Vue single-page-app HTML rather than JSON.

providers.name: data.gov.rs
providers.description: data.gov.rs is the national government open-data portal for the Republic of Serbia, operated by the Office for IT and eGovernment. It runs the uData platform and exposes the uData REST API over approximately 3,452 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, organization listings, and resource access. The API provides a consistent JSON-over-HTTP interface and is harvested into the EU data portal.

providers.name: dataset.gov.md (Portalul Datelor Deschise)
providers.description: dataset.gov.md is the national government open-data catalog for the Republic of Moldova (Portalul Datelor Deschise). The landing portal at date.gov.md links out to this catalog, which runs CKAN 2.10.4 and exposes the standard CKAN Action API over approximately 1,275 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. No API key is required for read endpoints.

providers.name: Synaptic
providers.description: Synaptic is a vertical AI solutions company that extends Salesforce and Agentforce environments with pre-built, industry-specific AI agents and applications. Its AQ Platform ships purpose-built agents for healthcare payers and providers (Provider AQ), government citizen services (Citizen AQ), and high-tech customer service (Service AQ), using a value-first methodology that promises measurable results within 30 days and full implementation within 90 days. Synaptic is a managed-delivery solutions and consulting firm rather than a self-service developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or technical documentation. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Ribbit Capital.

providers.name: AssetWorks
providers.description: AssetWorks is an enterprise fleet and asset management software company with more than 40 years of history and over 1,000 customers across commercial and private fleets, government and public works, and higher education. Its products include FleetFocus fleet and enterprise asset management (EAM), Active Assets fixed-asset tracking, Recoup Ops surplus management, and Scan and Validate mobile inventory management. AssetWorks sells on-premise and hosted enterprise software to large fleet and facility operators; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve API program. This repo is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Council on Environmental Quality
providers.description: The Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) is an office within the Executive Office of the President of the United States that coordinates federal environmental policy, advises the President on environmental and natural resource policies, and oversees the implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). CEQ does not publish a public developer API. Federal NEPA documents and related environmental data are surfaced through partner federal agencies and platforms (NEPAtool, the Federal Permitting Dashboard, regulations.gov, EPA EJScreen, and the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool).

providers.name: Govport
providers.description: GovPort is a Software-as-a-Service platform built specifically for government contractors (GovCons) to manage subcontractor performance, compliance, and collaboration. It centralizes critical contract records, sends primes and subs automated requirements to keep every party compliant, and lets GovCons securely share and manage deliverables with one another across teams. Positioned as subcontractor management software for the federal contracting ecosystem, GovPort emphasizes high levels of data privacy and security. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network; the company references APIs in its terms of service but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Flowbird
providers.description: Flowbird is a global urban mobility and parking technology company that builds pay stations, mobile parking apps, digital permits, EV charging, and transit ticketing systems for cities and transport authorities worldwide. Flowbird was acquired by EasyPark Group in an acquisition that closed in January 2025. Its integration surface is the Flowbird HUB, an open platform that exposes documented but partner/agency-gated APIs (OAuth2 and client-certificate secured, with role-based access control and ownership filters) for tariffs, rights/permits, parking sessions, pay stations, and transactions. There is no self-service public sign-up; access is granted to cities, transport agencies, and integration partners under contract.

providers.name: island.is (Digital Iceland)
providers.description: island.is (Stafrænt Ísland / Digital Iceland) is Iceland's national digital-services and government API platform, operated by the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs / Digital Iceland. It provides a GraphQL gateway at api.island.is (authentication-gated) that fronts internal REST microservices, with business/government-to-government REST services described using OpenAPI 3.0 and registered in the X-Road "Straumurinn" API Catalogue. The developer handbook is published at docs.devland.is. Iceland's former CKAN open-data portal (opingogn.is) has been decommissioned and now redirects to island.is.

providers.name: United States Africa Command
providers.description: United States Africa Command (AFRICOM) is a unified combatant command of the United States Department of Defense responsible for military operations and coordination in Africa. AFRICOM's primary mission is to advance U.S. national security interests and promote regional stability through security cooperation, military assistance, and joint training exercises with African partner nations. AFRICOM is headquartered at Kelley Barracks in Stuttgart, Germany and maintains relationships with 53 African nations. The command is led by a four-star general and conducts operations spanning humanitarian assistance, counter-terrorism, peacekeeping support, and capacity-building activities across the continent.

providers.name: Aurelius Systems
providers.description: Aurelius Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous directed-energy laser defense platforms for counter-unmanned-aerial-system (C-UAS) missions. Its flagship product, Archimedes, fuses high-power lasers, advanced optical sensing, and AI-guided autonomous tracking into a compact, field-deployable platform that detects, tracks, and neutralizes Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats at the speed of light and a fraction of the cost of traditional interceptors. The system runs on grid, generator, or commercial off-the-shelf batteries, is designed to operate without human operators, and can be networked into modular defensive grids to protect troops, bases, and critical infrastructure. Founded in 2025 by Michael LaFramboise and John Marmaduke, the company raised a $10M seed round co-led by General Catalyst and Draper Associates and is partnered with American Rheinmetall. Aurelius currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface — it is a directed-energy hardware company.

providers.name: Cx2
providers.description: CX2 is a defense technology company building AI-enabled electromagnetic spectrum (electronic warfare) systems for the tactical edge. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, CX2 develops attritable, machine-learning-powered hardware and software that detect, disrupt, and geolocate RF threats across land, air, sea, and space. Its flagship products are Wraith, a roughly 32-pound autonomous airborne EW platform that geolocates and identifies hostile emitters such as jammers and radars in GPS-denied environments, and Vadris, an RF-seeking payload for FPV drones that hunts ground control stations and other emitters of interest. CX2 is backed by 8VC, Point72 Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and sells directly to military and government customers. It does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: DEFCON AI
providers.description: DEFCON AI is a modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) company based in McLean, Virginia, building AI-driven optimization for contested logistics and mobility across defense and commercial operations. Founded in 2022, it develops mission-tailored optimization and intelligent-agent simulation products - including ARTIV (delivered to U.S. Air Force Air Mobility Command) and R-ALIGN for resilient multimodal logistics - that let planners rapidly generate and evaluate mission scenarios in dynamic, disrupted environments. The company was awarded a five-year, $115M prototype agreement supporting U.S. Marine Corps logistics modernization. DEFCON AI publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Overland AI
providers.description: Overland AI is a Seattle- and Washington, DC-based defense technology company building autonomous ground vehicle systems for military and national-security applications. Its product line spans ULTRA (a fully autonomous tactical vehicle with modular payloads), OverDrive (an off-road autonomy stack for tactical maneuver in GPS- and comms-denied environments), OverWatch (a command-and-control platform for single-operator control of multiple ground vehicles, which the company describes as offering an open API for integration with existing C2 systems), and SPARK (modular hardware that adds autonomous mobility to existing platforms). Overland AI is a portfolio company of 8VC. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; its "open API" is referenced only in marketing material and integration is handled through direct contact.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: United States Capitol Police
providers.description: The United States Capitol Police (USCP) is a federal law enforcement agency responsible for protecting the U.S. Capitol Building, members of Congress, and visitors to the Capitol complex. The agency is tasked with maintaining security and order within the Capitol grounds, conducting background checks on individuals entering the buildings, and responding to emergencies and threats. Capitol Police officers also provide security for large events and demonstrations taking place on Capitol Hill. As a legislative branch entity, the USCP operates under unique legal frameworks. In 2024, the agency adopted a FOIA-like request process making certain records publicly available upon request.

providers.name: Cork City Open Data
providers.description: Cork City Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Ireland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 32 datasets.

providers.name: SmartDublin Open Data
providers.description: SmartDublin Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Ireland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 929 datasets.

providers.name: EPA.gov
providers.description: EPA.gov is an alias for the Environmental Protection Agency entry. The canonical APIs.json index for U.S. EPA APIs and data services is maintained in the environmental-protection-agency repository, which catalogs EPA's Envirofacts Data Service, Air Quality System (AQS), UV Index, and ECHO Compliance and Enforcement APIs. Refer to the canonical record for current API listings, properties, and metadata.

providers.name: Birdstop
providers.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Center for Parent Information and Resources
providers.description: The Center for Parent Information and Resources (CPIR) is a federally funded central hub of information and products for the national network of Parent Training and Information Centers (PTIs) and Community Parent Resource Centers (CPRCs). CPIR supports families and youth, with a focus on children and youth with disabilities, delivering resources via the Parent Center Hub website, the Buzz from the Hub newsletter, and an events calendar. No public developer API has been identified; content and updates are delivered through website browsing, newsletter subscription, and an embedded Google Calendar.

providers.name: DOT Regulations
providers.description: Department of Transportation regulations governing the safe transportation of hazardous materials and other commercial transport activities in the United States. These regulations help organizations meet regulatory requirements and demonstrate accountability to stakeholders.

providers.name: opendata.gov.al (Open Data Albania)
providers.description: opendata.gov.al is the national government open-data portal for Albania (Open Data Albania). It is a custom, DCAT-AP-compliant platform (an Angular single-page-app front end over a bespoke REST API) with a dedicated SPARQL query endpoint, and it is harvested into the EU data portal (data.europa.eu). It is not CKAN or DKAN. Read endpoints live under the /api prefix using PascalCase, action-style routes.

providers.name: opendata.rks-gov.net (Kosovo Open Data) [offline]
providers.description: opendata.rks-gov.net (RKS Open Data) was the national government open-data portal for the Republic of Kosovo, historically running CKAN (~v2.7). As of mid-2025 the hostname no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) and the portal is offline; the last Internet Archive snapshots are from June 2025. It is cataloged here as historical pending restoration. Sectoral government open-data services remain available (e.g. Kosovo Customs at dogana.rks-gov.net/OpenData and the national geoportal at geoportal.rks-gov.net).

providers.name: National Gallery of Art
providers.description: The National Gallery of Art is a national art museum in Washington, D.C., located on the National Mall. The Gallery provides open access to images and data about its art collection through its Open Access program. While the Gallery does not publish a documented public REST API, it releases a comprehensive open dataset of more than 130,000 artworks and associated creators in CSV format under Creative Commons Zero licensing through its GitHub repository, with reconciled Wikidata Q-item identifiers for research interoperability.

providers.name: data.gov.mk
providers.description: data.gov.mk is the national government open-data portal for North Macedonia, operated by the Ministry of Digital Transformation. It runs CKAN and exposes the standard CKAN Action API over roughly 280+ datasets from 50+ public institutions, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access, plus DCAT exports (N3, TTL, XML, JSON-LD).

providers.name: Valthos
providers.description: Valthos is a New York City-based biodefense company developing frontier AI systems that identify biological threats and design medical countermeasures in real time. The company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $30 million in backing from the OpenAI Startup Fund, Lux Capital, and Founders Fund, with a founding team drawn from Palantir, DeepMind, the Broad Institute, and the Arc Institute. Valthos is building AI-powered biodefense infrastructure to rapidly analyze biological sequences and update medicines at scale for experts in government and the life sciences. The company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or open-source surface.

providers.name: Commission of Fine Arts
providers.description: The U.S. Commission of Fine Arts (CFA) is an independent federal agency established in 1910 that has review authority over the design and aesthetics of construction within Washington, D.C., and over coins, medals, and Federal commemorative works. The CFA also appoints the Old Georgetown Board which conducts design review for projects in the Georgetown Historic District. As of April 2026 the CFA does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specifications, or a developer program. Project records are accessible through the CFA's web-based Project Search tool and via the records-and-research process documented at cfa.gov.

providers.name: Kela Technologies
providers.description: Kela Technologies (kela.io) is a defense technology company founded by veterans of elite Israeli intelligence units, providing a secure, open platform that enables rapid and seamless integration of commercial and military systems in service of Western defense. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 after raising $39M from Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital, and In-Q-Tel (the CIA's venture arm). Kela is building "Sovereign Sky," a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation for resilient communication and navigation independent of foreign infrastructure, and acquired cloud-management company Pelanor. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single-page marketing site with a privacy policy but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Team Wildfire
providers.description: Team Wildfire develops jet engine-enabled fire suppression technology built to prevent catastrophic wildfire losses. Its mobile units, the "Hurricane" and "Storm Cell", apply fire retardant at scale to deny ground to advancing wildfires. The company offers fireground services, evacuation route hardening, asset protection, prescribed fire containment, and military base protection. Team Wildfire is a physical hardware and services company backed by Techstars; it publishes a marketing and services website but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals available for a non-API company.

providers.description: Toronto (CA) City Open Data

providers.name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
providers.description: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) is responsible for enforcing federal laws that make it illegal to discriminate against a job applicant or an employee because of the person's race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related conditions, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability or genetic information. EEOC publishes EEO-1, EEO-3, EEO-4, and EEO-5 workforce demographic data through the EEOC Explore data querying tool and downloadable bulk data files, but does not currently publish a public REST API for programmatic data access.

providers.name: Gallatin AI
providers.description: Gallatin AI builds AI-powered software for defense logistics, giving military planners and logisticians decision advantage across the tactical, operational, and strategic levels of the supply chain. Its products include Navigator, an AI decision-support "S4" that aggregates and analyzes brigade-level logistics reports in real time to streamline resupply planning; Burrow, a DoD-compliant third-party logistics (3PL) solution managing vendor qualification, transportation, inventory, storage, and fulfillment for domestic and international operations; and Phalanx, an automated asset and in-transit visibility system combining traditional reporting with hardware sensors and computer vision. Founded by veterans of Scale AI, Palantir, Amazon Prime Air, and the DoD, the company emerged from stealth in 2025 and is backed by 8VC, Silent Ventures, Timeless, Moonshots Capital, and Banter Capital.

providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

Its flagship product is Romulus, a constituent-relationship and case-management platform aimed at local and state government. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Joint Fire Science Program
providers.description: The Joint Fire Science Program (JFSP) funds scientific research on wildland fires and distributes results to help policymakers, fire managers and practitioners make sound decisions. Operated jointly by the U.S. Departments of the Interior and Agriculture, JFSP coordinates the Fire Science Exchange Network across regional knowledge nodes. JFSP does not publish a self-service developer portal or OpenAPI; research outputs are surfaced through the firescience.gov website.

providers.name: HUB Group
providers.description: HUB is a global leader in multifunction pole design and street infrastructure, supplying over 1,000 pieces of urban infrastructure worldwide. With 20+ years of experience, HUB excels in integrating digital devices and data analytics into innovative urban solutions. Partnered with Valmont Industries, HUB delivers high-quality infrastructure for public spaces, including telecommunications poles, monopoles, steel jackets, and head frames.

providers.name: National Institute of Mental Health
providers.description: The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) is the lead federal agency for research on mental disorders. NIMH conducts and supports research that seeks to understand, treat, and prevent mental illness, working to transform the understanding and treatment of mental illness.

providers.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
providers.description: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is a US federal agency that sets and enforces standards for safe and healthful working conditions. OSHA provides data APIs for accessing workplace injury and illness data, establishment inspection records, and compliance information.
