providers.name: Andrenam
providers.description: Andrenam is a defense technology company building an AI-powered maritime sensing network for undersea surveillance. It develops mass-manufacturable, low-cost buoy-based autonomous sonar systems that deploy from manned and unmanned vessels to detect, track, and identify real-time maritime traffic using cloud and edge AI, then dispatch resources to priority areas. Its product line spans deployment, AI-enhanced detection, and integration with naval command-and-control systems, targeting government and military maritime-domain-awareness customers. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Chaos
providers.description: CHAOS Industries is a U.S. defense-technology company founded in 2022 that builds advanced sensing and detection systems for military, border, and critical-infrastructure defense. Its Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN) technology powers a multi-product portfolio - including the Vanquish radar for early warning and tracking of unmanned aerial systems and missile threats, and HYDRA, a software-defined multi-application platform for detection, communications, and electronic effects. CHAOS markets domain dominance through counter-drone (counter-UAS) radar that detects threats up to ten minutes faster and tracks targets to 250 km. The company has raised roughly $1 billion from investors including 8VC, Accel, Valor Equity Partners, and NEA, with offices in Los Angeles, Washington DC, San Francisco, San Diego, London, and Amman. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; CHAOS publishes a marketing and newsroom presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: GreenQ
providers.description: GreenQ is an Israeli smart waste-management technology company (founded 2015, Jerusalem) promoting the "Internet of Garbage" — turning ordinary garbage trucks into smart trucks. Its GreenTrack device installs on any collection vehicle to weigh incoming waste and track route, mileage, capacity, time and per-bin (single-can-level) pickup data without requiring sensors on the bins, using a patent-pending visual-recognition algorithm. A recommendations engine then suggests route-optimization and scheduling improvements, surfaced through the GreenQ dashboard of reports and analytics. Collected data can be integrated with a municipality's local-authority systems through a private integration API; the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or specification. GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: L-3 Communications
providers.description: L-3 Communications was a U.S. defense prime contractor specializing in command, control, communications, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C3ISR) systems, aircraft modernization and maintenance, and government services. In 2019 L-3 merged with Harris Corporation to form L3Harris Technologies, which continues the legacy product lines and is now ranked among the top U.S. defense contractors. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: National Telecommunications and Information Administration
providers.description: The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) is an agency of the U.S. Department of Commerce that serves as the executive branch principal advisor on telecommunications and information policy issues.

providers.name: Obvio
providers.description: Obvio is an AI-powered traffic-safety platform that helps cities and police departments detect and enforce reckless driving. Its context-aware computer-vision cameras identify stop-sign violations, crosswalk failures, school-zone speeding, and distracted driving, then support law enforcement in reducing infractions and improving road safety. Obvio is a physical-AI company deployed with police departments in Maryland and expanding into new states; it is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Homebrew, and Khosla Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio lead; no public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: Smacktechnologies
providers.description: Smack Technologies is a frontier AI lab dedicated to national security, building domain-specific multimodal models trained via deep reinforcement learning in synthetic warfare environments to deliver decision dominance to the U.S. Department of War, its allies and partners. The company ships two product suites — Omega, a command-level AI stack pairing frontier models with customer-specific applications for strategic decision-making, and Alpha, an edge-level stack of lightweight models on proprietary hardware for tactical platforms and autonomous systems. Founded by MARSOC veterans Andrew Markoff and Clint Alanis and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Smack has raised $32M across Seed and Series A rounds led by Felicis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — a defense-domain vendor with no external developer surface.

providers.name: Vannevar Labs
providers.description: Vannevar Labs is a defense technology company building agentic AI for national security and 21st-century conflict, pre-trained for intelligence missions. Its product portfolio spans open-source intelligence and document exploitation (Decrypt, Serra, TIE, Curator), maritime domain awareness (Revere, Foreshadow), information operations (Overwatch, Local), and mission augmentation (Telescope), deployed across U.S. military bases and partner forces. Vannevar Labs operates as a sales-led, ITAR-restricted defense vendor and does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
providers.description: Booz Allen Hamilton is a leading management and technology consulting firm providing services primarily to U.S. government agencies in defense, intelligence, and civil markets. The firm employs over 2,500 AI specialists and 8,000 cybersecurity professionals, and maintains a significant open source presence on GitHub with projects including the Solutions Delivery Platform, Open Data Platform, and Cognition data fusion platform.

providers.name: Leidos
providers.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
providers.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy science and energy laboratory. ORNL provides public data and scientific computing resources for research including neutron science, materials science, computing, energy, and national security.

providers.name: BBN Technologies
providers.description: BBN Technologies is a research and development organization founded in 1948 (originally Bolt Beranek and Newman) and now operating as RTX BBN Technologies, a division of RTX (Raytheon). BBN is historically notable for pioneering the ARPANET, early network email, and packet-switched networking, and today conducts advanced defense and intelligence R&D across AI/machine learning, command and control, cyber operations, signal processing and spectrum, networking, quantum and photonics, and voice and language technologies. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery only.

providers.name: CH2M Hill
providers.description: CH2M Hill was a global engineering, consulting, design, construction and operations firm providing services for corporations and federal, state, and local governments. Headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, the firm delivered work in water, transportation, environment, energy, industrial, and facilities markets. In December 2017 CH2M was acquired by Jacobs Engineering (now Jacobs Solutions) and its operations have been integrated into Jacobs. As of the acquisition, CH2M Hill no longer publishes a standalone public API program; relevant digital engineering, project delivery, and data services are now offered under the Jacobs brand.

providers.name: Clausematch
providers.description: Clausematch is a London-founded regulatory technology (RegTech) company providing a cloud platform for policy and procedure management, regulatory change management, and structured document authoring and collaboration for banks, insurers, and other regulated financial institutions. Its tooling helps compliance teams draft, review, version, and attest to policies while mapping regulatory obligations to internal controls. Clausematch was acquired by Corlytics in 2024; the clausematch.com domain now 301-redirects to corlytics.com. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment (the web surface is WAF-protected and returns HTTP 403 to automated probes).

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: scytl
providers.description: scytl is an electoral technology company entered into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of balderton-capital and sapphire-ventures. The scytl.com domain today presents an electoral-technology offering (secure, scalable and auditable digital voting and election-management platforms serving governments and electoral bodies internationally). Enrichment probing found a live HTTPS site (TLS 1.3, SPF and DMARC with a reject policy) but no public API surface — no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/SDKs, or well-known API artifacts are published, so this profile remains an identity-and-security record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: ManTech International
providers.description: ManTech International is a Herndon, Virginia-based federal services contractor providing cybersecurity, data and AI, digital transformation, and intelligent engineering capabilities to U.S. defense, intelligence, and federal civilian agencies. Founded in 1968 and publicly traded on NASDAQ as MANT until 2022, the company was acquired by The Carlyle Group in April 2022 in an all-cash take-private transaction valued at approximately $4.2 billion and now operates as a Carlyle portfolio company. ManTech holds positions on major federal contract vehicles including Alliant 2/3, OASIS+, SeaPort NxG, CIO-SP3, T4NG, and ICON, and does not publish any developer-facing API or public OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Mississippi River Commission
providers.description: The Mississippi River Commission (MRC) is a federal agency established in 1879 that operates under the United States Army Corps of Engineers Mississippi Valley Division. The seven-member commission oversees the Mississippi River and Tributaries Project, managing flood control from the river's mouth to Cape Girardeau, Missouri, and improving navigation from Baton Rouge to Cairo, Illinois. The MRC is responsible for federal stewardship of the Mississippi River, including flood control, navigation, environmental management, and related engineering and policy work executed through six district offices.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Harris Computer
providers.description: Harris Computer is a constellation of companies acquiring and operating vertical market software businesses across the public sector, healthcare, utilities, financial services, education, and insurance markets. Harris Computer itself does not publish a unified public developer portal; APIs and integrations are delivered through its individual portfolio companies (such as Harris Local Government, Harris Utilities, Harris Healthcare, and Harris School Solutions). Harris Computer is a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc.

providers.name: National Security Agency
providers.description: The National Security Agency (NSA) is a U.S. intelligence agency responsible for global monitoring, collection, and processing of information and data for foreign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

providers.name: Faception
providers.description: Faception is an Israeli facial personality analytics company that applies proprietary computer vision and machine learning to analyze facial images from photos, video streams, and cameras, scoring individuals against personality and behavioral classifiers. The company markets its technology to public-safety and smart-city security, fintech, retail, insurance, recruiting, and personal-robotics use cases, and states that it analyzes faces anonymously by storing mathematical classifiers rather than personal identity data. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; at this time it publishes a marketing site and blog but no public API, developer documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Inversion
providers.description: Inversion is a Los Angeles-based aerospace and defense company founded in 2021 by Austin Briggs and Justin Fiaschetti, building a new class of highly maneuverable reentry vehicles. Its flagship Arc is an autonomous, reusable, low-cost space-based delivery vehicle designed to store cargo in orbit and deliver it with precision to anywhere on Earth in under an hour, descending under parachutes using non-toxic propellants so crews can approach it immediately on landing. The company also develops hypersonics and space-based interceptor technology and flew its first reentry capsule, Ray, as an early technical demonstrator. Inversion has raised roughly $54M to date, including a $44M Series A led by Spark Capital and Adjacent with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, Kindred Ventures, and Y Combinator. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rubicon
providers.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Office of Inspector General
providers.description: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) conducts audits, investigations, inspections, and other reviews to promote economy and efficiency in government programs and operations, and to prevent and detect fraud, waste, and abuse.

providers.name: Olea
providers.description: Olea is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: government. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Aerodome
providers.description: Aerodome was a Drone-as-First-Responder (DFR) company founded in 2023 by former California police officer Rahul Sidhu (CEO) and Kenaniah Cerny (Chief Architect). It built a fully integrated, automated, and remotely operated software platform that let public-safety agencies dispatch autonomous drones directly from 911 calls, pairing DJI drone hardware, robotic battery-swap docking nests, and radar with Aerodome DFR software featuring augmented-reality street overlays, automated flight operations, computer-aided-dispatch integration, and live airspace awareness. The company reported average 86-second response times to 911 calls. Backed by a16z, CRV, and 2048 Ventures across a seed (Oct 2023) and $21.5M Series A (May 2024), Aerodome was acquired by Flock Safety in October 2024 for over $300 million; its technology and software now ship as the Flock Safety "Flock DFR" product line, and the aerodome.com domain redirects to that product page.

providers.name: Basalt
providers.description: Basalt (Basalt Technologies Corp.) is a San Francisco spacecraft-software company building Dispatch, a simulation-based operating system for satellites that makes flight software portable across dissimilar spacecraft hardware — pitched as "Windows for spacecraft" and "Constellations as a Service." Dispatch provides a common control layer so fleets of different satellites can work together on tasking (visible, infrared, and radar imaging), in-orbit networking and telecom, signals intelligence, and monitoring or inspecting other on-orbit assets, including autonomous re-tasking for national security missions. Founded in 2023 by Max Bhatti and Alex Choi (ex-SpaceX engineers, MIT CubeSat program), Basalt is a Y Combinator W24 company that raised a $3.5M seed round led by Initialized Capital in May 2024, with participation from Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, and General Catalyst. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security. Sector: frontier-tech / space / defense.

providers.name: BBN
providers.description: BBN (RTX BBN Technologies, formerly BBN Technologies and Raytheon BBN) is an American research and development organization based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1948 and now a division of RTX Corporation. BBN has a storied history in computer networking, having built the original ARPANET Interface Message Processors and pioneered early email. Today it delivers advanced technology for national security across AI and machine learning, all-domain command and control, applied biosciences, cyber operations, spectrum dominance, maritime autonomy, multi-domain sensing, resilient networking, planning and logistics, quantum and photonics, and voice and language processing. General Catalyst has backed BBN since 2004. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency
providers.description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is the largest security agency in the federal government, dedicated to protecting America's trusted workforce and trusted workspaces. DCSA conducts personnel vetting and background investigations, oversees the National Industrial Security Program, delivers counterintelligence and insider threat support, and operates systems such as the Defense Information System for Security (DISS) and the National Background Investigation Services (NBIS). DCSA does not currently expose a public developer API; access to its mission systems is limited to authorized government users and cleared industry partners.

providers.name: Distributedspectrum
providers.description: Distributed Spectrum, self-described as "The World's First AI Signals Expert," builds edge-AI radio-frequency sensing technology that detects and identifies RF signals to autonomously map threats without expensive hardware or trained operators. Its sensors process data locally to deliver real-time alerts on threat types such as tactical radios, GPS jammers, and drones, and can be deployed anywhere using commercial components to form distributed detection networks. The company is headquartered at 99 Madison Ave, New York, NY, raised a $25M Series A, and is a Felicis portfolio company. No public API or developer program is published at this time; this profile carries the identity and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Evolv Technology
providers.description: Evolv Technologies Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: EVLV), headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, builds AI-based touchless security screening systems used to detect concealed weapons at venues, schools, hospitals, workplaces, and stadiums. Its flagship Evolv Express walk-through system uses sensor fusion and machine learning to screen people at high throughput without requiring them to stop, empty pockets, or remove bags, and the companion Evolv Insights analytics product reports on screening volume, alert rates, and operational performance. Evolv Technology is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, MCP server, or open developer portal; its public web presence is served behind bot protection and its status surface is gated behind SSO.

providers.name: Farm Credit Administration
providers.description: The Farm Credit Administration (FCA) is an independent federal agency responsible for regulating and supervising the Farm Credit System, a nationwide network of cooperatively owned institutions that provide credit and financial services to farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural borrowers. The FCA ensures that the Farm Credit System operates in a safe and sound manner and provides fair and competitive services. FCA does not publish a public REST API; however, the FCS Data Portal and downloadable Call Reports provide programmatic access to financial data on Farm Credit System institutions.

providers.name: Ghost Robotics
providers.description: Ghost Robotics designs and manufactures quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles (Q-UGV), with its flagship Vision 60 platform deployed across defense, public safety, law enforcement, industrial, construction, and education customers. The platform supports modular payloads for sensing, comms, and manipulation. Ghost Robotics provides a developer SDK only to vetted partners and integrators and does not operate a public developer portal, open API, or public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Greypoint Industries
providers.description: Greypoint Industries is a Canadian defense-technology company (Y Combinator S26) building passive RF mapping software that charts the electromagnetic spectrum so operators can see every signal, track every threat, and act first — "built in Canada for those who protect." Founded in 2026 by Nic Chu, Jordan Khoo, Steven Xu, and Darcy Zhang, the company also develops mass-produced autonomous counter-drone interceptors designed to defeat drone-swarm saturation at a fraction of the cost of the targets. As an early-stage hardware and software startup, Greypoint currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures the company's identity for the API Evangelist network and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: HawkEye 360
providers.description: HawkEye 360 is a Herndon, Virginia-based radio frequency (RF) data analytics and geospatial intelligence company that operates the first commercial satellite constellation purpose-built to identify, process, and geolocate a broad range of RF signals from space. Founded in 2015 by Chris DeMay, Charles Clancy, and Bob McGwier, the company flies clusters of three small satellites in formation that use time- and frequency-difference-of-arrival triangulation to pinpoint emitters across VHF through Ku-band. As of 2025, HawkEye 360 has placed 36 Hawk satellites on orbit across 12 operational clusters. Its core products include RFGeo (the underlying RF signal mapping and geolocation data product), RFIQ (its RF intelligence data product recently selected by NASA Commercial LEO programs), and Mission Space, a web-based RF geospatial intelligence analysis platform. The company also offers a Regional Awareness Subscription (RAS) service providing persistent monitoring of high-interest regions such as the Mediterranean, South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula. In December 2023 HawkEye 360 acquired Maxar Intelligence's RF Solutions business (formerly Aurora Insight), expanding its spectrum-mapping capabilities. Customers are concentrated in defense, intelligence, national security, and maritime domain awareness — including the US Government, allied partners, and foreign military sales (a 2025 FMS to India was approved by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency). HawkEye 360 has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO. There is no public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open-source release; data access is delivered through gated commercial and government contracts via the Mission Space platform and a customer-facing API for ordering and integration of RF analytics into customer systems.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. Enrichment note (2026-07-19): the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface, and its primary domain impossible.aero no longer resolves in DNS.

providers.name: Protent
providers.description: Protent is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a real-time video intelligence platform for law enforcement and public safety teams. Its software monitors many live surveillance, CCTV, and bodycam feeds at once, automatically prioritizing critical streams when escalation or volatility is detected, and lets teams run natural-language searches across active feeds (for example, "a person in a red hoodie with a backpack"). Founded in 2025 by Srihan Balaji (ex-Lockheed Martin Research, AWS) and Abhisheik Sharma (CTO, NLP/sentiment analysis), the company works with police departments in the Atlanta, Chicago, and St. Louis metro areas. As of this profile, Protent publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Singularity
providers.description: Singularity (Singularity Defense Corp) is a defense-technology company building low-cost, mass-producible air-defense and counter-weapon systems to protect warfighters and civilians from drones and cheap aerial munitions. Founded by engineers from SpaceX, Tesla, and Anduril alongside operators who have deployed air defenses in combat, the company emerged from stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with Menlo Ventures, NEA, Y Combinator, Harpoon Ventures, and others participating. It emphasizes in-house manufacturing of major subsystems combined with commercial-volume components for rapid production and field deployment, including active conflict zones. Singularity is a hardware defense company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Ursa Space Systems
providers.description: Ursa Space Systems is an Ithaca, New York-based geospatial intelligence company that turns commercial satellite data — primarily Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, combined with electro-optical, RF, AIS, and other ground-truth feeds — into decision-ready insight reports. The company operates a GeoAI platform branded "From pixels to insights" that fuses 90+ geospatial data sources and ingests imagery from a global network of commercial SAR and EO satellite operators, then applies in-house remote-sensing, data science, and GIS expertise to deliver answers about what is happening on the ground at specific places and times. Ursa Space serves U.S. Government customers — including U.S. Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) under INDOPACOM, AFRICOM, and SOUTHCOM, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) under the Luno A and Luno B delivery orders, the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), and humanitarian-aid agencies — as well as commercial enterprise customers in energy, commodities, supply chain, maritime, and insurance. Reporting domains span security and defense (border monitoring, military activity, maritime, dark-vessel and ship-to-ship transfer detection, airstrip monitoring), environmental and disaster response (deforestation, earthquakes, flooding, wildfires), and infrastructure and industry monitoring (construction, mining, oil and gas supply chain, power generation, space situational awareness). The platform is currently in beta and Ursa Space does not operate a public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, SDK, or self-service signup; engagement is sales-led through contact@ursaspace.com and tailored to government and enterprise contracts.

providers.name: Open Government, Romania
providers.description: Romania Government Open Data

providers.name: PRC Exam Schedule
providers.description: Unofficial Philippine Professional Regulation Commission's examination schedule

providers.name: National Cemetery Administration
providers.description: The National Cemetery Administration (NCA) is an agency of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs that provides burial and memorial benefits to veterans and their eligible family members. NCA does not currently expose a documented public REST API; access is via web tools such as the Nationwide Gravesite Locator and Cemetery Finder, with broader data available through VA Open Data.

providers.name: Navy
providers.description: The U.S. Navy plays a crucial role in defending national security and protecting the country's interests at sea. It operates a fleet of ships and submarines, as well as aircraft and personnel, to conduct a range of missions, including maritime patrol, reconnaissance, and combat operations. The Navy also performs humanitarian missions, such as disaster relief and search and rescue efforts. No public APIs have been identified at this time. The previously listed CNATRA "API" reference is an Aviation Preflight Indoctrination training video library, not a programmatic API.

providers.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
providers.description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is a federal agency responsible for regulating and supervising national banks and federal savings associations. The OCC ensures that these financial institutions operate in a safe and sound manner, comply with applicable laws and regulations, and treat customers fairly.

providers.name: Passports
providers.description: Index for tracking APIs, SDKs, and developer resources related to passports (travel documents, identity verification, and government issuance). No authoritative public passport API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board
providers.description: The Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board (FASAB) is an independent organization responsible for establishing accounting standards for the federal government. FASAB strives to improve the quality and consistency of financial reporting within federal agencies, ultimately ensuring transparency and accountability in government financial operations.

providers.name: Federal Maritime Commission
providers.description: The Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) is an independent agency of the United States government responsible for the regulation of international ocean transportation. The FMC oversees the practices of ocean common carriers, marine terminal operators, and other regulated entities.

providers.name: National Capital Planning Commission
providers.description: The National Capital Planning Commission is the federal government's planning agency for the National Capital Region. The Commission works with federal agencies to preserve and enhance the historical, cultural, and natural resources and federal assets of the National Capital Region. No public developer API has been identified at this time; available access is through the public website, project search, and FOIA.

providers.name: National Endowment for the Arts
providers.description: The National Endowment for the Arts is an independent federal agency that funds, promotes, and strengthens the creative capacity of our communities by providing all Americans with diverse opportunities for arts participation. NEA does not currently expose a documented public REST API; arts and culture data is available through partner programs such as the Arts and Cultural Production Satellite Account (with BEA) and the Survey of Public Participation in the Arts (with the U.S. Census Bureau).

providers.name: National Laboratories
providers.description: The U.S. Department of Energy's national laboratories are a network of federally funded research and development centers conducting cutting-edge research in energy, science, and national security.

providers.name: V2X
providers.description: V2X is a defense and national security contractor providing mission-critical solutions including AI integration, cybersecurity, advanced engineering, operations support, training, and modernization services. The company serves U.S. government, allied defense, and aerospace customers globally. V2X does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Cyren Call
providers.description: Cyren Call Communications Corp. was a wireless communications company founded in 2005 by Nextel co-founder Morgan O'Brien to advocate for a nationwide public-safety broadband network. Its central proposal asked the FCC to reallocate 30 MHz of 700 MHz-band spectrum (freed by the 2009 analog-TV shutdown) to public-safety users, and it later served as advisor to the Public Safety Spectrum Trust (PSST) after PSST became the nationwide licensee for public safety's 10 MHz of 700 MHz broadband spectrum. The FCC dismissed Cyren Call's original petition as inconsistent with auction requirements, and the PSST advisory relationship ended in early 2009. The company is permanently closed. It never operated a developer program, public API, or SDK surface, so no API artifacts are available for enrichment.

providers.name: Govlist
providers.description: Govlist, Inc. (which operated as ProcureNow) was a San Francisco-based govtech startup providing a multi-tenant SaaS platform for government procurement and contract management. Its Government Procurement Automation Cloud helped local and state agencies build, source, and evaluate RFPs and bids, and helped suppliers read, understand, and respond to complex public solicitations. The company, backed by 500 Global and Civstart, was acquired by OpenGov in 2021 (announced June 2021), where the product now lives as OpenGov Procurement. Govlist has no independent developer surface, API, or portal; its original domain (thegovlist.com) no longer resolves. This profile is preserved as a historical lead surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio.

providers.name: Justinian
providers.description: Justinian is an applied AI company, backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), building what it calls the first AI-native government affairs firm. Founded by Parth Badhwar (previously Clipbook, The White House, Deloitte's policy team, and the Harris campaign), Justinian helps early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts. The firm operates from San Francisco and Washington, DC, pairing staff drawn from the White House and top lobbying firms with engineering, and frames its mission as rebuilding public-private partnerships in America. Justinian currently presents as a services and product company with a demo-request/contact flow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Modria.com
providers.description: Modria is an online dispute resolution (ODR) platform originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Enrichment (2026-07-20) confirmed the company is no longer independent; the modria.com domain 301-redirects in full to www.tylertech.com/solutions/modria, so Modria now operates as a resolution/ODR solution within Tyler Technologies. No independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or .well-known discovery surface exists on modria.com (every path redirects to the Tyler Technologies marketing page). Retained as a network record; there is no standalone API to enrich.

providers.name: Silver Spring Networks *
providers.description: Silver Spring Networks was a smart-grid, smart-city, and IoT networking company that built wireless canopy networks and the SLV/Data Platform for utilities, offering RESTful Data Platform APIs (device registration, device metadata, sensor data, and webhook event notifications) plus an SDK on its developer portal at developer.ssni.com. Itron completed its acquisition of the company in January 2018 for approximately USD 830 million and rebranded it Itron Networked Solutions; the standalone ssni.com and developer.ssni.com properties are now offline. Enrichment pass 2026-07-21 found no live API surface: all legacy domains fail to resolve and the historical developer portal is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Director of National Intelligence
providers.description: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence leads intelligence integration and forges an intelligence community that delivers the most insightful intelligence possible. The ODNI serves as the head of the intelligence community, overseeing and coordinating the foreign and domestic activities of the US intelligence community.

providers.name: Economic Development Administration
providers.description: The U.S. Economic Development Administration (EDA) is an agency in the United States Department of Commerce that provides grants and technical assistance to economically distressed communities in order to generate new employment, help retain existing jobs and stimulate industrial and commercial growth through a variety of investment programs. EDA works with boards and communities across the country on economic development strategies.

providers.name: Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology
providers.description: The Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) is an interagency committee dedicated to improving the quality of Federal statistics. FCSM is hosted under the federal Statistical Policy Office and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Federal Laboratory Consortium for Technology Transfer
providers.description: The Federal Laboratory Consortium for Technology Transfer (FLC) facilitates knowledge and technology sharing across federal laboratories, and speeds the adoption of new knowledge and technologies in the wider economy by facilitating the sharing federal research with non-governmental public and private entities.

providers.name: Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission
providers.description: The Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission is an independent adjudicative agency that provides administrative trial and appellate review of legal disputes arising under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Amendments Act of 1977 (Mine Act).

providers.name: Federal Protective Service
providers.description: The Federal Protective Service uses its security expertise and law enforcement authority to protect federal government facilities and safeguard the millions of employees and visitors who pass through them every day.

providers.name: Foreign Claims Settlement Commission
providers.description: The Foreign Claims Settlement Commission of the United States (FCSC) is a quasi-judicial, independent agency within the Department of Justice which adjudicates claims of U.S. nationals against foreign governments.

providers.name: National Indian Gaming Commission
providers.description: The National Indian Gaming Commission (NIGC) is an independent federal regulatory agency that regulates gaming on Indian lands to protect tribal gaming as a means of generating revenue for tribal governments. The agency publishes online resources, public records, and gaming-related data through its website but does not currently expose a public web API.

providers.name: National Institute of Corrections
providers.description: The National Institute of Corrections (NIC) is an agency within the U.S. Department of Justice that provides training, technical assistance, and information to federal, state, and local corrections agencies. NIC publishes guidance, library resources, and corrections-related data through its website but does not currently expose a public web API.

providers.name: Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education
providers.description: The Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education is a government agency that focuses on providing resources and support to individuals seeking to further their education and career opportunities. This office offers programs and initiatives that are designed to help adults acquire the skills and knowledge needed to succeed in the workforce.

providers.name: Office of Government Ethics
providers.description: The Office of Government Ethics (OGE) is an independent agency within the federal government that oversees the behavior and ethics of executive branch employees. The OGE provides guidance and advice on ethics laws and regulations to government officials, conducts ethics training programs, and reviews financial disclosure reports to ensure compliance with ethical standards. The office also works to prevent conflicts of interest and promote transparency and accountability in government operations.

providers.name: Forest Service
providers.description: The Forest Service is an agency within the U.S. Department of Agriculture that is responsible for managing the nation's forests and grasslands.

providers.name: Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service
providers.description: The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) provides mediation and other conflict resolution services for managing and enhancing labor-management relationships.

providers.name: IZOIC’s
providers.description: IZOIC’s is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: government. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Outil Achats
providers.description: Outil Achats refers to French procurement and purchasing tools used by public and private sector organizations for managing tenders, suppliers, and contracts. No verifiable public APIs are currently documented for this category.

providers.name: Mine Health and Safety Administration
providers.description: The Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) works to prevent mining related deaths, injuries, and illnesses through mine regulations, inspections, and training programs.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Costanoa Ventures
providers.description: Costanoa Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in June 2012 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with an additional office in San Francisco. Costanoa invests primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, writing checks of roughly $1M to $10M and taking concentrated 10-15% ownership across about 35 companies per fund. The firm's thesis is to fill the "missing middle" of early-stage venture by providing unusually hands-on, operator-led support to founders building applied AI, AI and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security / defense tech, fintech, and enterprise software companies. Costanoa was founded by Greg Sands (an early Netscape product manager) and manages roughly $2.8B in assets. In September 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Fund V at $275M alongside Opportunity Fund III at $119M, doubling down on AI-enabled B2B technology. Portfolio companies include Alation, Cyberhaven, Quizlet, PayNearMe, Auterion, Vannevar Labs, Kepler Communications, and Muon Space.

providers.name: Export-Import Bank of the United States
providers.description: The U.S. Export-Import Bank (EXIM) is the official export credit agency of the United States federal government. It assists in financing and facilitating U.S. exports of goods and services by providing export credit insurance, working capital guarantees, and direct loans to help American businesses compete in the global marketplace. EXIM publishes open government data including authorization records accessible via the federal Data.gov catalog using the Socrata Open Data API (SODA).
